title: Bounded-below derived counit detected on cohomology sheaves
statement: Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),R)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] with sheaves of commutative rings on sites small in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their ordinary unbounded derived categories with cohomology $H^q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose module pullback $f^*$ is exact. Write $f^*=Lf^*$ for its termwise derived functor and $Rf_*$ for total right derived direct image, computed by K-injective resolutions, with their canonical derived adjunction unit $\eta:1\to Rf_*f^*$ and counit $\varepsilon:f^*Rf_*\to1$. Let $K\in D(\mathcal O)$ satisfy $H^q(K)=0$ for all $q<a$ for some integer $a$. If $\varepsilon_{H^q(K)[0]}:f^*Rf_*(H^q(K)[0])\to H^q(K)[0]$ is an isomorphism for every integer $q$, then $\varepsilon_K:f^*Rf_*K\to K$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$. The sites are small in the module universe, so these are Grothendieck abelian categories admitting K-injective resolutions. Exactness of module pullback gives a triangulated termwise functor $F_D=f^*:D(\mathcal B)\to D(\mathcal A)$, with the canonical shift comparisons. Its cohomology comparison is $H^q(f^*M)\cong f^*H^q(M)$: represent $M$ by a complex and apply the exact-functor cohomology lemma. Hence $f^*$ preserves every standard lower cohomological bound, including negative bounds.

source.place: Tag 0D7S (lemma-bounded-in-image-upstairs), exact pullback in its cohomology comparison; homology.tex Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor).

proof.text: The K-injective total right derived functor $Rf_*$ is triangulated by the right-derived-functor lemma. Apply clause (1) of the exact-derived-adjunction bounds lemma with $F=f^*$, $F_D=f^*$ and $R_D=Rf_*$. The required termwise factorization was established in step 1, and $f^*\dashv Rf_*$ is the canonical adjunction in the hypothesis. Thus $Rf_*$ preserves every standard lower cohomological bound. Consequently $\Phi=f^*Rf_*$ and $\Psi=1$ restrict to triangulated endofunctors of $D^+(\mathcal A)$, and both preserve every lower bound.

source.place: Tag 0D7S, comparison with the upper truncation; derived.tex Tag 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing) and Tag 0A8D (lemma-adjoint-is-exact).

proof.text: The module pullback and direct image have their underived adjunction. Its left adjoint is exact by hypothesis, its right adjoint is additive, and its target module category has K-injective resolutions by step 1. The canonical-right-derived-adjunction shift lemma therefore applies to this very adjunction: its derived counit $\varepsilon:\Phi\to\Psi$ commutes with the canonical shifts, retaining the K-injective shift on $Rf_*$. Restricting to $D^+(\mathcal A)$ retains this compatibility and the given counit components.

source.place: Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint); derived.tex Tag 0A8D (lemma-adjoint-is-exact), canonical counit shift comparisons used in Tag 0D7S.

proof.text: Apply the bounded-below heart test with both abelian categories equal to $\mathcal A$, with $\Phi,\Psi$ from step 2, transformation $\varepsilon$ from step 3, and object $E=K$. Boundedness below is exactly $H^q(K)=0$ for $q<a$, and the heart-test hypothesis on $\varepsilon_{H^q(K)[0]}$ is precisely the assumption of the item. All its functor and shift hypotheses have been verified. It gives invertibility of $\varepsilon_K$. Explicitly, for every integer $m$ it gives an invertible $\varepsilon_{\tau_{\le m}K}$ and invertible degree-$m$ images of $c_m:\tau_{\le m}K\to K$ under both functors, with $H^m(\varepsilon_K)=H^m(c_m)\circ H^m(\varepsilon_{\tau_{\le m}K})\circ H^m(\Phi(c_m))^{-1}$. This is the degreewise truncation comparison of Tag 0D7S; the heart test packages its finite Postnikov induction. Its conclusion includes $m<a$ and requires no upper bound or infinite-limit preservation.
